cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's tax machine prepare Form 941, the quarterly payroll tax return, for HANGS General Contracting.
First, it reads the returns already filed this year. Pay since January shows who has reached the Social Security wage limit.
Next, the quarter's payroll. The payroll register lists every paycheck: 560 of them, for 96 employees. It also reads the tax deposits and the general ledger, the company's main accounting record.
Now it checks the official tax rules online: tax rates, the Social Security wage limit and deposit deadlines. All sixteen checks are confirmed, and one question is left for a person.

Then it works out the return. Withholding is the tax taken out of each paycheck; the employer adds its own matching share. Schedule B lists the tax owed on each payday. The quarter's total is $690,018, and the deposits cover it in full.
Twelve checks pass: every paycheck and the ledger agree to the cent.
Last, it writes the draft return and its workpapers, the math behind every figure.

All done. The draft shows just over $690,000 of tax for the quarter, all deposited, so nothing more is due. Two items stay open: whether one worker paid as a vendor is really an employee, and the filing date that depends on it. A person reviews and signs before anything is filed.
